Label: ^(nozzle|print(ing)?|extrusion|extruder|hot ?end)\s*temp\w*(\s*[-(]?\s*(standard|high)\s*speed\)?)?|^nozzle(?!\s*(material|type|diameter|size))\b
Note: a sheet that prints two speeds prints two nozzle rows; the first is the standard one. A table with a temperature column names the setting alone ("Nozzle 230-260°C"), and the value must still state a temperature

Label: ^(bed|heat ?bed|heated bed|build plate|platform|table|plate)\s*temp\w*|^heat ?bed\b
Note: a table with a temperature column names the bed alone; a sheet may call the heated bed the plate: Plate Temp.

Label: ^(closed|enclosed)\s*(chamber|space|build ?(chamber|volume))|^(chamber|enclosure|housing)
Note: a chamber statement with no temperature of its own is about the enclosure

Label: ^(build plate|print(ing)? (surface|plate)|bed surface|plate)\s*(material|treatment|surface)?\b
Note: the row may name what the plate is made of or what it is coated with: Plate Material / Plate Treatment

Label: ^(drying|dry)\s*(temp\w*|conditions|settings|parameters|recommendations)|^dry(ing)? before
Note: a sheet may abbreviate it: Drying Temp.

Label: ^(ruby or hardened nozzle|hardened nozzle|abrasion[- ]resistant nozzle|nozzle (type|material))
Note: 'Abrasion resistance' is a measured property (ISO 4649), not a statement about the nozzle

Label: ^(print(ing)? )?speed|^(max\.?|maximum)?\s*volumetric\s*(flow\s*)?(speed|rate)?
Note: a maximum volumetric speed is a limit on the print speed and the register keeps it as speed guidance
